name: Paramānanda Purī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Uddhava**, Kṛṣṇa's friend and minister, «accepted by Kṛṣṇa as his equal», whom He sent to Vraja with His message — and who stays in Vraja for ever.

## Gopāla-campū — Uddhava

- **Who he is** (Uttara-campū 10.12, verses 1–4): Kṛṣṇa thought: «Uddhava who realized something of my childhood pastimes while worshiping me during his childhood and who developed sickness by hiding his prema for me during his kaiśora age is here with me!» «I constantly desire the association of Uddhava—who studied under Bṛhaspati the authorized scriptures on conduct… who experiences the whirling nature of prema for me, and who is most suitable to be my minister.» «He is different from the Yadus and different from Balarāma. I inquire from him on all topics at all times.» «**My soul is present externally as Uddhava.** My mind and his mind operate in the same way and not otherwise.»
- **Why him** (10.11): Kṛṣṇa needed a messenger «who understands my sweetness and majesty… If he only understands my sweetness, he will be burdened by the anguish of their intense grief. If he only understands my majesty, he will consider their absorption in my sweetness to be improper behavior.»
- **Sent to Vraja** (10.14): «he took Uddhava's tear-soaked hand in his tear-soaked hand» and said: «na tathā me priyatam ātma-yonir na śaṅkaraḥ… yathā bhavān» — not Brahmā, Śiva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Śrī or His own self are as dear to Him as Uddhava (SB 11.14.15). His visit to Vraja and the gopīs fills Uttara-campū 10–12.
- **The gopīs' foot-dust** (Pūrva-campū 15, verse 3): «Uddhava, who was accepted by Kṛṣṇa as his equal, has said that the glory of the gopīs cannot compare to anything and offered respects to the dust of their feet.»
- **For ever in Vraja** (Uttara-campū 37.23, verse 8): «Though it is proven that Kṛṣṇa and others, through their expansions, reside in Vraja, it is suitable that Uddhava also does. Since he had prayed to take birth among the shrubs of Vraja, he should attain that goal for he is the assistant of the gopīs, Vṛndāvana and Kṛṣṇa. The gopīs are Uddhava's goal. Vṛndāvana is the abode of the gopīs. Kṛṣṇa is the master of Vṛndāvana.»

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.3; Uttara 10.11–14 (verses 1–5), 37.23 (verse 8).

name: Śrī Keśava Bhāratī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Sāndīpani Muni**, Kṛṣṇa's and Balarāma's teacher in Avantī — and **Akrūra**, who took Them from Vraja to Mathurā.

## Gopāla-campū — Sāndīpani

- **Why him** (Uttara-campū 8.15): «A person who is fixed in Brahman and worships Śiva would be the best guru. The great soul Sāndīpani of a dynasty from Kāśī is a worshiper of Śiva.»
- **The two students** (8.19–22): «they went to the assembly of Sāndīpani who was blissful with all knowledge»; «Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma entered into the assembly of Sāndīpani resplendent with thousands of brāhmaṇas, like the sun and moon entering the sky with Jupiter» (verse 22). «Filled with strong devotion… as they held fire wood in their hands and begging for knowledge, they impressed Sāndīpani.» «Greeting them, Sāndīpani said, “Time for study is very rare. O dedicated students! I will keep you here for a long time to study”» (verse 29); «Giving up your identity as kṣatriyas, you must first learn how to beg with the brāhmaṇa students.» Then Kṛṣṇa brought back his guru's son (Uttara-campū 9).

## Gopāla-campū — Akrūra («Cruelty of Akrūra», Uttara-campū 2)

- **Seeing Their footprints** (2, verse 13): «When Akrūra from far away saw just their foot prints, attractive as painted pictures, he became completely bewildered.» «Akrūra saw Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa as two young elephants among the calves. One had blue cloth and the other had cloth yellow like lightning» (verse 20).
- **Their welcome** (2.19–22): Kṛṣṇa «raised Akrūra up with his two spread arms. Akrūra, with choked voice, could not even utter his name.» «The two boys, pained by Akrūra's confusion, forgot to treat him as an uncle and respected him by embracing him.»
- «Meeting respectful Akrūra, Nanda remembered the suffering caused by Kaṃsa, and, praising Akrūra's qualities, removed all that suffering by his blessings. Though Akrūra and Vasudeva were gentle, on remembering the cruelty of Kaṃsa my mind becomes disturbed» (verse 23).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 2.13–24 (verses 13–23), 8.15–22 (verses 22–29).

name: Kāśī Miśra
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Kubjā** (Trivakrā), the hunchbacked servant-girl of Kaṃsa in Mathurā whom Kṛṣṇa made straight.

## Gopāla-campū — Kubjā (Uttara-campū 4)

- «Seeing Kubjā with a hunchback going to the bathing ghaṭa made of crystal carrying some cosmetics, Kṛṣṇa asked for the cosmetics and smeared it all on his body. The cosmetics also made his friends effulgent. He then straightened out Kubjā's body, amazing everyone with his great qualities» (verse 21).
- «If there is no bhakti, straightness is only an external show. If one has internal bhakti, the straightness will show externally. Kubjā is the example» (verse 22).
- Her words: «O beautiful-faced man! I am a servant… Kaṃsa's… my name is Trivakrā» (4.51–55). In Vraja Lalitā asked, «Why was virtuous Kubjā a hunchback, since for those with good character anything is possible?» (4.45).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the three kinds of love

«Madhura-rati is of three types: sādhāraṇī (general), samañjasā (divided) and samarthā (competent). Sādhāraṇī-rati is ordinary rati. This is seen in the hunchbacked girl Kubja. It is as difficult to attain as an ordinary jewel. Queens like Śrī Rukmiṇī and Śrī Satyabhāmā possess samañjasā-madhura-rati, which is likened to a transcendental touchstone. Only the gopīs of Vraja possess samarthā-madhura-rati, which is just like the Kaustubha jewel.» «When rati for Kṛṣṇa is characterized by desiring one's personal happiness… it is known as sādhāraṇī-rati. When rati for Śrī Kṛṣṇa has the feeling that ‘He is my husband and I am His wife' and aims to achieve happiness for both Śrī Kṛṣṇa and oneself, it is known as samañjasā-rati» (Rati-bheda, p. 35).

> kubjāyāṁ sādhāraṇī ratiḥ prema-paryantā | paṭṭa-mahiṣīṣu samañjasā-ratiḥ anurāga-paryantā | tatra satyabhāmā rādhikānusāriṇī lakṣmaṇā ca | rukmiṇī tu candrāvalī-bhāvānusāriṇī (Āśraya-nirṇaya, text 15)

«Kubjā has sādhāraṇī-rati up to the stage of prema. The samañjasā-rati of the Dvārakā queens extends to the stage of anurāga. Among them, Satyabhāmā and Lakṣmaṇā bear some resemblance to Śrīmatī Rādhikā from the perspective of form, qualities and moods of contrariness. In the same way, Rukmiṇī and the other queens bear some resemblance to Candrāvalī in regard to form, qualities and nature» (pp. 45–46).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 4.33–55 (verses 21–22); Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Rati-bheda (p. 35), Āśraya-nirṇaya 15 (pp. 45–46).

name: Lakṣmīpriyā Mātā
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Rukmiṇī**, the first queen of Dvārakā, daughter of Bhīṣmaka — in Vraja she was Candrāvalī, says the Gopāla-campū.

## Gopāla-campū — Rukmiṇī's marriage (Uttara-campū 16)

- **The brāhmaṇa's message** (16.5): «There is a king named Bhīṣmaka living in Kuṇḍina in Vidarbha state. He is the abode of great fame… He has some demonic sons like Rukmī and a daughter named Rukmiṇī. Friends who know the king's heart were thinking of offering her to you. But Rukmī has deceived them and has attempted to give her to Śiśupāla. This praiseworthy daughter, hearing of your qualities… has already accepted you in her mind… Giving up shyness, she has sent me to you.» Her words: «One should not be ashamed for a righteous cause… Those women are fortunate who worship Kṛṣṇa because of attraction, giving up local custom and dharma» (verse 1).
- **Waiting** (16.27–29): the brāhmaṇa «stayed awake all night thinking of auspicious subjects. Rukmiṇī was thinking that the brāhmaṇa would» come; «By closeness to the brāhmaṇa who was fragrant with the aroma of Kṛṣṇa, Rukmiṇī became fragrant. She experienced such strong joy within» (verse 14); bowing to him, «she made him most exalted».
- The people of Vidarbha prayed: «Let strong, lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa accept the lotus hand of Rukmiṇī» (16.33); «Rukmiṇī worshiped Durgā according to the proper method» before Kṛṣṇa took her away (16.36).
- **The queens were the gopīs** (Uttara-campū 17, verse 53): «Candrāvalī was Rukmiṇī. Rādhā was Satyabhāmā. Viśākhā was Kālindī. Lalitā was Jāmbavatī. Śyāmā was Lakṣmaṇā, Śaibyā was Mitravindā, and Bhadrāvalī was Bhadrā. Padmā was Satyā. They were almost equivalent in nature.» «Though they were of the same nature, they were not exactly equal in giving happiness to Kṛṣṇa. As rubbing oil on the feet soothes the eyes, so when he enjoyed with the queens, the gopīs felt some relief, because of some identity» (17.196).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the three kinds of love

«Madhura-rati is of three types: sādhāraṇī (general), samañjasā (divided) and samarthā (competent). Sādhāraṇī-rati is ordinary rati. This is seen in the hunchbacked girl Kubja. It is as difficult to attain as an ordinary jewel. Queens like Śrī Rukmiṇī and Śrī Satyabhāmā possess samañjasā-madhura-rati, which is likened to a transcendental touchstone. Only the gopīs of Vraja possess samarthā-madhura-rati, which is just like the Kaustubha jewel.» «When rati for Kṛṣṇa is characterized by desiring one's personal happiness… it is known as sādhāraṇī-rati. When rati for Śrī Kṛṣṇa has the feeling that ‘He is my husband and I am His wife' and aims to achieve happiness for both Śrī Kṛṣṇa and oneself, it is known as samañjasā-rati» (Rati-bheda, p. 35).

> kubjāyāṁ sādhāraṇī ratiḥ prema-paryantā | paṭṭa-mahiṣīṣu samañjasā-ratiḥ anurāga-paryantā | tatra satyabhāmā rādhikānusāriṇī lakṣmaṇā ca | rukmiṇī tu candrāvalī-bhāvānusāriṇī (Āśraya-nirṇaya, text 15)

«Kubjā has sādhāraṇī-rati up to the stage of prema. The samañjasā-rati of the Dvārakā queens extends to the stage of anurāga. Among them, Satyabhāmā and Lakṣmaṇā bear some resemblance to Śrīmatī Rādhikā from the perspective of form, qualities and moods of contrariness. In the same way, Rukmiṇī and the other queens bear some resemblance to Candrāvalī in regard to form, qualities and nature» (pp. 45–46).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 16.5–36, 17.53, 17.196; Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Rati-bheda (p. 35), Āśraya-nirṇaya 15 (pp. 45–46).

text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Satyabhāmā**, Kṛṣṇa's proud queen in Dvārakā, daughter of Satrājit — in Vraja she was Rādhā, says the Gopāla-campū.

## Gopāla-campū — Satyabhāmā

- **Her father's gift** (Uttara-campū 17.62–64): Satrājit, fearing Kṛṣṇa's anger over the jewel, thought «By giving my jewel of a daughter, even more valuable, along with this jewel, I will satisfy him», and «he gave his daughter named Satyabhāmā along with the jewel… Satyabhāmā's bhakti was unlimited and she had natural attachment to Kṛṣṇa.»
- «Hear the amazing incident how Satyabhāmā from childhood would see Kṛṣṇa through the lattice holes in the terrace» (verse 9).
- **The pārijāta** (Uttara-campū 18.25–52): «This was the opportunity for fulfilling the promise Kṛṣṇa made to Satyabhāmā to get her a pārijāta tree. Among all of his beloved queens, he proposed to give the tree to her. Mounting Garuḍa with Satyabhāmā, Kṛṣṇa… went to Prāgjyotiṣa.» «Satyabhāmā, seeing those extra arms, touched them and, covering her mouth with her cloth, began to laugh»; «he made Satyabhāmā's hairs stand on end for fun» (verse 12).
- **The queens were the gopīs** (Uttara-campū 17, verse 53): «Candrāvalī was Rukmiṇī. Rādhā was Satyabhāmā. Viśākhā was Kālindī. Lalitā was Jāmbavatī. name: Sanātana Miśra
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**King Satrājit**, Satyabhāmā's father, the owner of the Syamantaka jewel.

## Gopāla-campū — Satrājit (Uttara-campū 17)

- «Satrājit, who performed sacrifices to please the sun, having pleased the sun» received the jewel (17.13); proud, he «does not offer the jewel to Kṛṣṇa» (17.16).
- When the jewel was found, Kṛṣṇa «called Satrājit to the assembly with respect. After relating all that had happened, he finally gave the jewel to him with a smile» (17.59). «First the jewel turned away from Kṛṣṇa and then turned face downwards (in shame) to Satrājit» (verse 7).
- «Satrājit began to think, “Kṛṣṇa is secretly angry with me. How can I satisfy him?… By giving my jewel of a daughter, even more valuable, along with this jewel, I will satisfy him.”» «He gave his daughter named Satyabhāmā along with the jewel… Satyabhāmā's bhakti was unlimited… His lack of devotion has been described» (17.62–64).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 17.13–64 (verses 7–8).

name: Sūryadāsa Sarakhela
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**King Kakudmī** (Revata), the father of Revatī, whom he gave to Balarāma.

## Gopāla-campū — Revata Kakudmī (Uttara-campū 15)

- «I am Revata, also known as Kakudmi. Having heard of the many ancient kings, you must have heard of me. With my youthful body I went past Svarga up to Brahmaloka… Seeing my daughter's extraordinary qualities and not seeing a suitable groom, I went to Brahmā to arrange a suitable person… Brahmā… said, ‘What is a short time here is a kalpa on earth… But I realize this: Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa's elder brother, will make her happy'» (15.19–20).
- «‘She is very tall. How can she be his wife?' Brahmā said, ‘The older brother of Kṛṣṇa, who straightened out Kubjā, can do this'» (verse 6).
- Kṛṣṇa «welcomed Revata in the city and after consulting with Vasudeva and others, he got Balarāma to agree to their decision. Balarāma then took his plough in the night and while she was sleeping, altered her limbs, making her happy. Kṛṣṇa then performed their marriage» (15.27).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 15.19–28 (verse 6).

name: Jagannātha Ācārya
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Durvāsā Muni**, who proved the gopīs' purity before their wedding with Kṛṣṇa.

## Gopāla-campū — Durvāsā

- **At the gopīs' wedding** (Uttara-campū 32.68–79): before the wedding feast, when the elders feared for the gopīs' honour, «By her mind, Paurṇamāsī then called Durvāsā, who arrived wearing bark as his dress. Though he shone because of his austerities, when he goes to the Himalayas, his ferocious nature disappears.» He said: «I am Durvāsā, whom everyone fears. I am the giver of fear. Kṛṣṇa who gives unconditional benefit to all, should be considered the supreme shelter.» «Having gone to the outskirts, Durvāsā, taking on the form of fire, by his effulgence turned the place into ashes. The gopīs entered the fire and spread their hands to Durvāsā. In bliss, they remained cool like the Gaṅgā and made everyone peaceful» (verse 26). Then «making Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma happy, Durvāsā disappeared… what more need be said about the purity of the gopīs?»
- **His word to the gopīs** (Uttara-campū 8.46, 31.33): «Durvāsā revealer of the Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad has revealed this (He said, “He will be your husband.”)»; «When the gopīs ask a question in Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Durvāsā says, “He is your husband.”»

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 8.46, 31.33, 32.68–79 (verse 26).

name: Jagannātha Paṇḍita
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Durvāsā Muni** — so said the notes of this record; the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā (111) gives Durvāsā to Jagannātha Ācārya (Gaṅgādāsa). What the Gopāla-campū says of Durvāsā:

## Gopāla-campū — Durvāsā

- **At the gopīs' wedding** (Uttara-campū 32.68–79): before the wedding feast, when the elders feared for the gopīs' honour, «By her mind, Paurṇamāsī then called Durvāsā, who arrived wearing bark as his dress. Though he shone because of his austerities, when he goes to the Himalayas, his ferocious nature disappears.» He said: «I am Durvāsā, whom everyone fears. I am the giver of fear. Kṛṣṇa who gives unconditional benefit to all, should be considered the supreme shelter.» «Having gone to the outskirts, Durvāsā, taking on the form of fire, by his effulgence turned the place into ashes. The gopīs entered the fire and spread their hands to Durvāsā. In bliss, they remained cool like the Gaṅgā and made everyone peaceful» (verse 26). Then «making Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma happy, Durvāsā disappeared… what more need be said about the purity of the gopīs?»
- **His word to the gopīs** (Uttara-campū 8.46, 31.33): «Durvāsā revealer of the Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad has revealed this (He said, “He will be your husband.”)»; «When the gopīs ask a question in Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Durvāsā says, “He is your husband.”»

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 8.46, 31.33, 32.68–79 (verse 26).

name: Śuklāmbara Brahmacārī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

The **wives of the brāhmaṇas** (*yajña-patnīs*) who brought food to Kṛṣṇa in the forest.

## Gopāla-campū — the brāhmaṇas' wives (Pūrva-campū 22)

- Kṛṣṇa «desired to show mercy to the wives of the brāhmaṇas engaged in sacrifice» (22.2); He told His friends: «Those without pride do not execute dharma as the proud people do… go to the wives of the brāhmaṇas» (verse 11).
- «Their hearts had melted in affection by his attractive rāgas using the skillful, sweet notes of the flute… by seeing his qualities, form and pastimes, and by their tears» (verse 12). «Since their desire to see Kṛṣṇa had previously been thwarted, their hearts had been broken. Then Kṛṣṇa sent his friends who were like his very life… How could the wives maintain their self-control?» (verse 15).
- «Putting the unlimited boys in front, the wives, placing the food vessels on their heads, went to Kṛṣṇa. With anxiety, at every step they uttered, “How much further?”» (verse 17). «Kṛṣṇa was wandering blissfully with his friends in an aśoka forest on the bank of the Yamunā. The wives saw him in this condition and thought, “The object of our meditation has become visible to our eyes today”» (verse 19).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 22.2–33 (verses 11–19).
